key_insight: Charge separation in low-offset organic solar cells is governed not just by the LE–CT energy gap, but also by exciton-CT hybridization, state degeneracy, and Gaussian disorder, which can either hinder or help efficiency depending on the offset regime.
engineering_relevance: The results give a design rule for organic photovoltaics: tuning molecular energetics and disorder can preserve or improve charge separation even when the LE–CT offset is near zero.
method: Compared a macroscopic two-state rate model against 3D kinetic Monte Carlo simulations.
Varied the LE–CT energetic offset and the ratio of LE/CT degeneracies.
Added Gaussian energetic disorder to test how thermalization affects charge separation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the rate model matches kMC across the full offset range without disorder, and that disorder shows a crossover: harmful at large offsets but beneficial at intermediate and low offsets.
watch_item: The disorder-assisted efficiency gains depend on the specific energetic landscape and state degeneracies, so the conclusions may not transfer directly without material-specific parameter calibration.
paper_title: Dependence of charge separation efficiency on the exciton-charge transfer offset and Gaussian disorder in organic solar cells
